title: Size of the move (4/4): code runs the look-first sequence (Surveys, then scoping) at both recommendation seams
description:
## As asked

Piece 4 of 4 of LIN-4346 ("Deciding the size of the move becomes part of the run"). Lands last, and only once piece 3's pre-registered replay has passed.

**Why.** Today a person starts both Surveys by hand and writes the scope by hand. LIN-4346's Done-when: a ticket John files goes from filed to building with no one writing its scope by hand, and the size it chose, and why, reads plainly on the ticket. The look-first step stays advice, not a gate, with no review loop of its own (`docs/plans/survey.md`).

**This piece's slice of the approved plan**

* **One code-route helper at both seams.** Generalise `loopBoundRecommendation` (`lib/openrouter.js`) into one helper that tries the review-loop bound, then the look-first sequence. Call it from both `getRecommendation` and `getRecommendationStream`; trace which route fired. The streamed path emits a complete recommendation with no model call, as the loop bound does today. Recommend-and-dispatch therefore dispatches it.
* **Eligibility (all must hold):** an As-asked block; a leaf; not completed/canceled; no size record (piece 2's parser), no plan, no PR; no open blocker (`issue.blockedBy` non-terminal); the newest run is not waiting on a person; no person's comment holding it. The sequence starts at the earlier of the first run and the first Survey comment. Person comments (`isPersonComment`) before that are filing context and never turn the route off. A person comment after the start holds the route until a run **dispatched** after that comment exists (by `dispatchedAt`; a run merely finishing afterwards does not release it). Headed comments, including John's `## Size of the move (the person's call)` rulings, are not person comments and never hold; scoping reads them as rulings. State this next to the hold rule.
* **Step choice:** survey-task → survey-place → scoping, each attempted once. A Survey counts as attempted when its comment exists or any run of its kind is on record, whatever its status/outcome; scoping when a size record exists or any scoping run is on record. Once all three are attempted, stand aside for the selector (so failed scoping with no record falls through once, never loops).
* **Attempts source:** refactor `loadRecentRuns` (`lib/recent-runs.js`) to return, from the same single store read, the unsliced run list for attempts and the existing 5-run slice for the selector. The history read is up to 20 dispatch rows before filtering, plus live rows; say "20 rows", not "20 stage runs", in the residual-risk wording. Selector prompt bytes unchanged by this refactor.
* **Open decisions from completed runs (verdict note 1; engineering choice, record the reason):** a `DECISION:` raised by a run that ended `done` does not read as "waiting on a person". Either use `openDecisionLoopIds` to hold the route if it is cheap from the recommendation path (no new store read just for this), or state exactly in the plan text and restated invariant that remaining look-first steps may proceed once each and read that ruling. Witness either way: a run that ended `done` with an open `DECISION:`.
* One constant per Survey comment heading, read by both template (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`) and route. Survey `route` stays `null`: the route reads only whether a step happened, never what it said.
* Scoping's `route.when` gains: a size ruling has been answered and the record still reads pending. Regenerate `tests/fixtures/stage-router-prompts/` on purpose and review the diff.
* **Hand-only claims:** update the Survey template descriptions and comment, `lib/prompt-templates.js`, `lib/run-view.js`, `public/llms.txt`, `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md`, the `lib/stage-router.js` rule comment, and `tests/unit/lin-4248-survey-stages.test.js` (the router refusal stays true). Re-run `grep -rn -i -E "hand-triggered|hand-only|never routed|by hand" lib public docs/architecture CLAUDE.md` with `survey`; any new hit is in scope.
* **Restated invariant** in CLAUDE.md (edit in place; 110-line cap), `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md`, and the stage-router comment: code settles only the review loop bound and the look-first sequence; neither reads a model's verdict; a person's comment posted after work started outranks the look-first sequence until a later dispatched run.
* `docs/plans/survey.md` "How the choice is made": under the policy, larger or just the task goes ahead; smaller than asked or wrong work gets a ruling; with no policy every size is a ruling. Note how to read Survey cost per ticket (`GET /issues/{id}/cost`, by kind).
* **In-flight tickets at merge (verdict note 5):** re-read LIN-4348 and LIN-4358 before merging and update LIN-4346's in-flight paragraph to match. Approved behaviour: one scoping attempt converts a headed size comment into a guarded ruling record when still eligible; any ticket with a plan is untouched.

**Testing strategy / witness** (unit tests, each failing before the change)

* Unsized leaf, empty trail → survey-task; with that comment → survey-place; with both → scoping.
* "Before you start" comment and no runs → survey-task (LIN-4347/4350 shape).
* Ended survey-task run with no comment moves on, not re-sent. Scoping run ended with no record → route returns nothing; same for queued/running/waiting scoping.
* Person comment after a Survey run, no later run → route off; resumes once a later run is dispatched. Comment posted mid-run, then that run ends → still held. A Survey's own headed comment never holds.
* Plan, PR, size record, children, no As-asked block, completed/canceled, open blocker, newest run waiting → each off; resolved blocker → not off. Completed run with open `DECISION:` → per the choice above.
* Opposite Survey verdicts → same route.
* Pending record + answered ruling: facts line reads "pending a ruling" and scoping's `when` covers it.
* LIN-4348 shape (Survey comments, headed size comment, no record) → unsized, gets scoping once nothing holds it.
* Parity: same ticket through `getRecommendation` and `getRecommendationStream` gives the same code-routed step; recommend-and-dispatch dispatches it. A code-routed Survey dispatch shows by kind in `GET /issues/{id}/cost`.
* After merge, on LIN-4346: observe John's first tickets with `err-larger` set reach building with no hand-written scope and a plain size record.

**Session fit:** fits one session.

**Plan-review due:** no — covered by LIN-4346's approving plan-review (comment d71c7085-b2ad-4760-8070-53bc917f9a1f, rev 1).

**Grounding commit:** `11dc1d7bd` (`origin/main` when the plan was written and reviewed; still `origin/main` at breakdown, 7 Nov 22:45 UTC).

**Starting point:** LIN-4346's approved plan is this piece's starting point. Read it in full in LIN-4346's description under `## Implementation Plan` (revision 1), with the builder notes in the approving verdict (comment d71c7085, 22:42). Read LIN-4346's `## As asked` block for the person's words and John's comment of 22:18 for the size ruling (err larger). Follow the plan; where the code shows it wrong, change course and say so on LIN-4346.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Outcome (close-out, 8 Nov)

**Implemented and merged:** PR [#2370](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2370>), merge commit `f0388614c`, deployed. One code route at both recommendation seams: the review-loop bound first, then the look-first sequence (survey-task, then survey-place, then scoping, each attempted once).

The plan slice above was implemented as approved, with one deviation, agreed by John's ruling `lin4370-live-scoping-wait` (answered `wait`): the route hands back to the selector only once all three steps are attempted **and none is live**. While a step is live, it waits (`lookFirstWait`; recommend-and-dispatch answers 409 `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT`).

**Discharged here:**

* The LIN-4369 requirement: scoping's final message never reaches the stage after it, and the size record does. Witnessed in `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js`.
* The merge gate: LIN-4369 was Done before the merge.

**Still open after the deploy (on named monitors; see the close-out comment):**

* The end-to-end witness on a new John ticket.
* The inherited LIN-4369 cut-path check on the first live record with non-`none` Cuts.

**Follow-ups:** LIN-4392 (cross-kind dispatch guard) and LIN-4388 (selector rule 1 dating).

The full history (the requirement from LIN-4369, the merge gate, and earlier stage text) is preserved in the task snapshots and the comment trail.

comments.body:
## Unblock: LIN-4370 can be built now, and merges only after LIN-4369 is Done

**Blocker type:** a stale dependency hiding an external outage. The `blocks` relation from LIN-4369 stood for "lands last, only once piece 3's replay has passed". That gate is met: the replay passed (arm 4, 10:20), LIN-4369 merged as `d294a190` (confirmed on `origin/main`), and its close-out says "Piece 4 may begin, carrying it" (ledger item 1, already appended to this description).

**Root cause of the stall:** LIN-4369 stays In Progress only because production has not deployed it, so its two post-deploy checks (the cut path and the no-policy path) cannot run. `harbour-cat` is still on `110e35e0` (site footer). Seven builds in a row have failed in Railpack's setup step fetching `mise` from GitHub releases with a 503. I retried once at 11:40 with `railway redeploy -s harbour-cat --from-source`, following LIN-4369's named next action. Deployment `ac892d8f` failed the same way, although the same URL returned 200 from this machine. GitHub's incident ("Increase in timeouts for some unauthenticated users") is still open. Nothing here is code. The running deployment is untouched.

**Options**
1. Keep the relation and wait for GitHub. Nothing to do, but the cost of doing nothing is that piece 4 sits idle for an unknown time, although building it needs nothing from the deploy.
2. **Drop the relation, build now, gate the merge (chosen).** Building is reversible and needs only main. The real ordering constraint is the merge: this piece makes scoping run automatically, so it should not ship before LIN-4369's live checks. That gate is now written in the description ("Merge gate").
3. Change the Railway build so it stops downloading `mise` at build time (pin or cache it, or move to a Dockerfile). This would address the outage at its source, but it changes production infrastructure, so it is the team's call and out of this ticket's scope. Worth raising only if GitHub stays degraded.

**Done:** removed `blocks` LIN-4369 → LIN-4370 (relation `3e756387`), set this ticket to In Progress, and appended the merge gate and a re-grounding note to the description. The grounding commit `11dc1d7bd` is stale: about a dozen merges since have touched `lib/openrouter.js`, `lib/stage-router.js`, `lib/prompt-template-defs.js` and `CLAUDE.md`, which is now at exactly its 110-line cap. Nothing in the As-asked block is cut, so there is no `DECISION:`.

**Next action:** dispatch the build for LIN-4370 against main HEAD. Separately, once a `harbour-cat` deploy of `d294a190` or later succeeds, re-run LIN-4369's close-out. Its Done releases this ticket's merge.

**Worth knowing now, not blocking:** production's standing size policy reads "Ask each time" (LIN-4369 ledger item 3), while LIN-4346's As-asked block gives "err larger". Once this piece lands, every ticket routed automatically stops at a size ruling until that is set in Settings → Running. This piece's after-merge witness ("John's first tickets with `err-larger` set") depends on it.

## Implementation: LIN-4370 (PR open, CI green; merge held for LIN-4369)

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2370, commit `7a4446eed`. `ci-success` is green: unit, all four E2E shards and the secret scan.

**Merge gate.** Do not merge until LIN-4369 is Done. At 12:15 UTC LIN-4369 was still In Progress: it is merged, but the deploy has not landed, so its cut-path and no-policy checks have not run. The PR body starts with this gate.

**What landed.** A fresh leaf with an As-asked block and no size record, plan or PR now runs survey-task, then survey-place, then scoping. Code sends each step once and asks no model. The route lives in `lib/recommendation-look-first.js`. One helper, `codeRoutedRecommendation`, serves both seams. It tries the review loop bound first, then the look-first sequence, and the prompt trace records which one fired. So recommend-and-dispatch sends the same step the task page streams.

The route stands aside when any of these holds:
- the ticket has an open blocker;
- its newest run is waiting on a person;
- the run read failed;
- a person's comment posted after the sequence started has no run dispatched after it yet (by `dispatchedAt`).

Comments filed before the sequence started never hold it, and neither do headed comments. Once all three steps have been attempted, the selector decides, so a failed scoping run falls through to it once. Scoping's `route.when` now also covers a size ruling answered while the record still reads pending.

**Engineering choice (verdict note 1).** An open `DECISION:` from a run that ended `done` does not hold the route. The remaining steps proceed, at most once each, and read that ruling on the trail. Holding on it would mean calling `openDecisionLoopIds`, which needs whole loops. This ticket's run read does not carry them, so it would take a new store read. The choice is stated in the module, in `prompt-system.md` beside the invariant, and in LIN-4346's plan text, which I edited. A witness test covers it.

**Handoff (LIN-4369 ledger item 1).** Scoping's final message never reaches the routing prompt or the dispatched prompt; I tested this through the real recommend-and-dispatch route. The size record does reach the routing prompt, its facts line and the brief, and the build prompt points the builder to that brief.

**In-flight tickets (verdict note 5).** I re-read both and updated LIN-4346's in-flight paragraph:
- LIN-4358 has PRs on its trail, so the route leaves it alone.
- LIN-4348 has no As-asked block yet, so the route is off for it. Its first dispatch adds the block and releases its 10:15 comment; the next recommendation then sends scoping once.

Check both again at merge.

**Evidence.**
- Unit suite: 24,493 pass, 0 fail on the branch, against 24,465 pass, 0 fail on base `f8b946d40`. The extra 28 are new tests.
- The 27 tests in `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js` fail before the change. I removed the route from the seams, and under eight targeted mutations, each test failed on the mutation it targets.
- The routing prompt grew by 96 bytes. Each budget raise is recorded with its reason.

**Cuts:** none. The after-merge observation still needs someone to set `err-larger` in Settings → Running, which reads "Ask each time" in production today.

### Leftovers

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2370, head `9a7849df780b01407c11269fb5c2b42918af5e33`. `ci-success` is green: unit, all four E2E shards and the secret scan. Unit suite: 24,541 pass, 0 fail after merging main.

- `lib/recommendation-facts.js` called the review loop bound "the one route code settles". It now says it is the first of two. **Tidied.**
- `tests/unit/next-stage-choice.test.js` had the same claim in a describe title. **Tidied.**
- `docs/architecture/prompt-system.md` said "Code settles one route itself". It now reads "two routes". **Tidied.**
- `lib/recent-runs.js` header said the read was for the selector only. It now says the same read feeds the look-first route. **Tidied.**
- **Lesson: not added.** Both notes it could go in are at their 6,144-byte cap since main moved:
  - `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` is at 6,118 bytes;
  - `docs/areas/runs-and-dispatch.md` is at about 6,070 bytes;
  - neither has an entry my change makes stale.

  The rule is "run facts carry no run's messages; that keeps scoping's report out of later prompts". The handoff test in `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js` already pins it.
- **For close-out (a pre-existing defect, outside this change):** selector rule 1 reads runs by their `at` time, and for an ended run `at` is when it ended. A person's comment posted while a run was going can therefore read as already acted on. This is the same flaw verdict note 3 fixed in the look-first route (which reads `dispatchedAt`). Fixing it changes the selector facts and the routing prompt bytes, so it needs its own ticket.
- **Merge note:** main had moved, and `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` conflicted, which stopped CI from starting on the leftover push. I merged main, took main's version of the note, and re-ran the suite and CI.

Merge gate unchanged: hold until LIN-4369 is Done.

**LIN-4369 is Done** (merged as `d294a190`, deployed; production is on `ab942e80`). This ticket's merge gate on LIN-4369 being Done is now met.

Two post-deploy checks from LIN-4369's review ledger did not run, because no live scoping record exists yet. The first live scoping run will most likely come from this ticket's seam, so whoever reviews or closes out this ticket should run them on that first record:
1. **Cut path (ledger 2):** on the first live scoping record whose Cuts line is not `none`, `GET /api/proxy/rulings?issueIdentifier=<that ticket>` shows a scoping `DECISION:`, and Decided by is not `the standing policy` unless the cut bullet names a person's ruling.
2. **No-policy path (ledger 3):** the live scoping render reads "no standing policy" today (Settings → Running = **Ask each time**). While that holds, the first live record must say `pending a ruling` and its run must raise a `DECISION:`.

Rollback for LIN-4369, if either check fails: revert merge commit `d294a190`. Your existing requirement still stands: the routing seam must not hand scoping's final message to a building stage.

## Review — LIN-4370

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2370, reviewed at head `9a7849df780b01407c11269fb5c2b42918af5e33`. Since then main has gained one commit (`ab942e800`, LIN-4358 docs). Close-out should re-check CI on the exact head it merges.

CI: green on `9a7849df7` (`CI success`, unit tests, E2E shards 1–4 and secret scan all pass).

### Against what was asked (in order)
- **One code-route helper at both seams.** Met. `codeRoutedRecommendation` / `codeRouteOf` (`lib/openrouter.js`) tries the loop bound first, then `lookFirstStep`. `getRecommendation` and `getRecommendationStream` both call it. The trace now stores `codeRoute` (`blocked` / `look-first`); `prompt-trace-store.js` used to drop that field. All three routed surfaces (`routes/proxy.js:1540`, and `modelCallArgs` and the stream in `routes/workspace-api.js`) build their input with `prepareRecommendationInput`, so all of them get `allRuns`. The wired recommend-and-dispatch test covers this.
- **Eligibility.** Met, clause by clause, in `lookFirstOff`. A failed run read (`allRuns: null`) turns the route off, which is a reasonable addition that fails safe. The rule that a breakdown child still gets the sequence matches LIN-4346's plan ("Breakdown children are leaves too … John accepts the cost"). `issue.blockedBy` is the same field the routing prompt already reads (`openrouter.js:732`). The hold rule, its use of `dispatchedAt`, and the note that headed comments never hold all sit together in `holdingComment`, as asked.
- **Step choice / attempted-once / stand aside after three.** Met (`attempted`, `LOOK_FIRST_STEPS`).
- **Attempts source.** Met. `loadRecentRuns` makes one read and returns `{runs, allRuns}`. `selectorSlice` strips `dispatchedAt`, so the selector's lines and bytes are unchanged. The wording says "20 rows". The LIN-3364 `closed`-stamp fix is still in place in `runFact`.
- **Open decisions from completed runs.** Met. The second option was chosen (no new store read), with the reason recorded in the module, `prompt-system.md` and LIN-4346's plan. A witness test covers it.
- **One heading constant.** Met: `SURVEY_HEADINGS` is read by both templates and the route. Survey `route` stays `null`.
- **Scoping `route.when`.** Met. The six router fixtures and the eval baseline were regenerated. The routing prompt grew by 96 bytes, recorded beside the ceiling.
- **Hand-only claims.** Met. I re-ran `grep -rn -i -E "hand-triggered|hand-only|never routed|by hand" lib public docs/architecture CLAUDE.md | grep -i survey`. The only remaining hits say "or by hand", which is true.
- **Restated invariant.** Met in CLAUDE.md (edited in place, still 110 lines), `prompt-system.md` and the `stage-router.js` comment.
- **`docs/plans/survey.md`.** Met: the policy, cut and no-policy cases, plus how to read Survey cost by kind.
- **In-flight tickets.** Done at build time. It has to be repeated at merge (ledger).
- **Witness list.** Every listed test exists in `tests/unit/lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js`, all 27 pass, and 48 pass across the three touched test files.

### Mutation check (LIN-2274)
I made each change below to the code, ran `lin-4370-look-first-route.test.js`, and reverted:
- `sentAt` uses `at` instead of `dispatchedAt` → 1 failure.
- Hold removed → 4 failures.
- Blocker check removed → 1. Any blocker counted as open → 1.
- Waiting check removed → 1.
- A Survey comment no longer counts as attempted → 3.
- `runs unknown` guard removed → 1.
- PR check removed → 1.
- `sequenceStart` ignores Survey comments → 1.
- Stream seam bypasses `codeRoutedRecommendation` → 4.
- `loadRecentRuns` returns `allRuns: null` on success → 3.

Every mutation turned the suite red, so the load-bearing tests are wired into the real path.

### Regression check
`git log` since 7 Nov 22:46 on the touched files shows LIN-4358, LIN-4369, LIN-4367/4368 and LIN-4374/4376. None of them is reverted or re-broken here. The PR merged main and kept main's version of `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
- **Parallel sends while a look-first step is live.** A queued or running Survey counts as attempted, and nothing on recommend-and-dispatch stops a different kind while a run is live: the duplicate guard (`lib/dispatch-factory.js` `guardDuplicate`) is keyed by issue **and kind**. I checked directly. `lookFirstStep` with a running `survey-task` returns `survey-place`. With `survey-task` running and `survey-place` queued, it returns **`scoping`**. If anything calls recommend-and-dispatch on a ticket while its Surveys are still live, scoping runs before either Survey comment exists, which defeats "a following step then reads both notes" (LIN-4346 As asked). The selector path has the same property for every stage (no live-run guard across kinds), so the class predates this PR. This route is the first place where it costs the deliverable's own claim. **Inside** (a claim the ticket depends on). Ledger item 2.
- **The selector's rule 1 reads `at` (end time) where it should read dispatch time.** The builder found this. It is the same idiom verdict note 3 fixed in the look-first route, but on the selector's facts, and fixing it changes the routing bytes. **Outside**: the selector's own defect, not this ticket's. Close-out files it after checking it is not already filed.

### Leftovers (edges, not defects)
- `lib/recommendation-look-first.js:63` re-spells the outcome literal `'waiting on a person'` that `lib/recent-runs.js` `runFact` produces. No shared constant links the two, so renaming one silently disables the "newest run waiting" off-switch. Inside the area and fix-sized: **close-out fixes it on the PR branch**. Export `const WAITING_ON_A_PERSON = 'waiting on a person'` from `lib/recent-runs.js`, use it in `runFact`, and import it in `recommendation-look-first.js` in place of the local `WAITING`.
- The builder's Leftovers comment lists four tidies, and I confirmed each one in the diff. The builder added no lesson because both notes files are at their cap, and the handoff test pins the rule. I accept that.
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` Waiting entry on `lib/prompt-formatters.js` (the area-notes pointer for scoping and the Surveys). This PR does not change the scoping or Survey prompt bodies, so the entry is still accurate and untouched. No action.

### What CI Did Not Prove
1. **Merge gate: LIN-4369 must be Done.** *Inside* (the ticket's own constraint). As of this review, LIN-4369 is still **In Progress** (`completedAt: null`). **Before the merge:** close-out reads LIN-4369's state. If it is not Done, close-out holds and does not merge.
2. **Scoping must not be dispatched while a Survey run is queued or running.** *Inside* (the parent's "reads both notes"). **Before the merge:** close-out finds out whether any routed caller (the autopilot or its lanes, or Go on the task page) calls recommend-and-dispatch on a ticket that has a queued or taken stage row.
   - The exact repro is `lookFirstStep(leaf, { allRuns: [survey-task running, survey-place queued] })` → `scoping`. Then recommend-and-dispatch on such a ticket, and check whether a `scoping` row is enqueued beside the live Survey rows.
   - If no caller does this in practice, record why and the item is discharged.
   - If any does, this is **Request Changes back to implementation**. The fix is in `lookFirstStep`: when the next step is `scoping` and a Survey run is `queued`/`running`, do not send scoping. It also needs a decision on what the route returns instead. Returning null hands the ticket to the selector, which can pick another stage in parallel. That design choice belongs to implementation, not close-out.
3. **In-flight tickets at merge.** *Inside* (verdict note 5). **Before the merge:** re-read LIN-4348 and LIN-4358 and bring LIN-4346's in-flight paragraph up to date. Correct state: LIN-4358 keeps a PR on its trail, so the route is off. LIN-4348 stays off until it has an As-asked block, then gets scoping once nothing holds it.
4. **Production's standing size policy reads "Ask each time", not `err-larger`.** *Inside* (the after-merge witness depends on it). **After the deploy:** someone has to set Settings → Running to `err-larger` before the witness is read. John is the natural owner. Otherwise every automatically routed ticket stops at a size ruling, which is correct no-policy behaviour but not the witness asked for.
5. **After-merge witness.** *Inside*. **After the deploy:** the first of John's new tickets, with `err-larger` set, goes survey-task → survey-place → scoping → building with no hand-written scope and a plain size record. Close-out also confirms the two Surveys appear by kind in `GET /issues/{id}/cost`. **Named monitor:** the prompt-trace store's `codeRoute: 'look-first'` entries for that ticket. There should be exactly one per step, and a second entry for the same step on the same ticket is the re-send failure. This only shows up in production because the 20-row history window and real comment timing cannot be reproduced in CI.
6. **Residual risk: more than 20 dispatch rows before sizing.** *Inside* (stated in the module). In that case a Survey that ran without posting could run again. **Named monitor:** the same `codeRoute` trace check as item 5.
7. **Rollback.** Revert the merge commit of #2370. Nothing is persisted in a new shape: `codeRoute` is an extra nullable trace field, and size records are written by LIN-4369's code, not this PR's. So the change is reversible.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

Close-out must make one fix: the `WAITING_ON_A_PERSON` constant described under Leftovers. Ledger items 1–3 must be settled before merging. If item 2 shows that a routed caller sends while a Survey is live, the verdict becomes **Request Changes**, back to `implementation`.

## Close-out — LIN-4370

**Not merged. The task stays open. Next: `implementation`.** Ledger item 2 failed when I ran it on the real dispatch path. Review's verdict says that turns into **Request Changes** back to implementation, and the fix needs a design choice (what the route returns instead), so it is not close-out's to make.

PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2370. Head is now `94123340d` (was `9a7849df7`).

### Change made (the one fix review asked for)
- `94123340d`: export `WAITING_ON_A_PERSON` from `lib/recent-runs.js`, use it in `runFact`, and import it in `lib/recommendation-look-first.js` in place of the local `WAITING` literal. This answers review Leftovers bullet 1. The touched suites pass locally: 70 pass, 0 fail (`lin-4370-look-first-route`, `recent-runs*`, `next-stage-choice`). CI was re-triggered on `94123340d`. Secret scan passed; unit and E2E were still pending when this was posted. There is nothing to merge, so it is not a gate now.

### Ledger
1. **LIN-4369 Done:** **settled.** I read its live state: Done, `completedAt` 2026-11-08T13:28:53Z.

## Implementation (ledger item 2): no step is sent while another is live

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2370, head `7ee9c8d986f4202f90726415b8cd5c20a13a573c` (fix commit `dcec1154a`, then a merge of main). **CI green on that head:** `CI success`, unit tests, E2E shards 1–4 and the secret scan.

### The defect, at its cause
A live Survey counted as "attempted", so the route moved on to the next step. Nothing on the server blocks a different kind: `guardDuplicate` is keyed by issue and kind, for 5 minutes.

### What the route does instead (the design choice close-out asked for)
While a look-first step is **queued or running**, the route answers **wait**. It also waits while any other stage run is live and a look-first step is still to come. A wait sends no step, and it does **not** hand the ticket to the selector: the selector has no cross-kind live-run guard, so standing aside would only move the parallel send there.
- **Both seams:** the prompt is null; `codeRoute` is `look-first-wait`; `lookFirstWait` is `{kind, id, dispatchedAt, outcome}`. No model call. The trace names the wait separately, so the after-deploy monitor (`codeRoute: 'look-first'`, one per step) is not polluted.
- **recommend-and-dispatch:** returns **409 `LOOK_FIRST_IN_FLIGHT`** with the live dispatch's `id` to adopt, the same pattern as `DUPLICATE_DISPATCH`. The task page stream sends the same refusal as its error event.
- **Autopilot "re-dispatch fresh" on a wedged look-first step:**
  - abort it (`abort` + `abortTo` the id), then call recommend-and-dispatch again; the aborted step counts as attempted, so the next step goes;
  - or, to re-run the step itself, re-send it with the `kind` override.

  This guidance is in the 409 body, `lib/proxy-instructions.js` and `docs/proxy-integration.md`. The kickoff prompts are unchanged; the autopilot reads it from the refusal.
- **A run nobody ends keeps the wait.** Age alone never ends a run. The wait stays visible, with its id, until someone aborts it.

### Departure, stated for review
The ask said: "Once all three are attempted, stand aside for the selector." I narrowed that to "...and none is live": a **live scoping** run is also waited on, so the selector cannot start a build before the size record exists.
- The witness still holds: `lookFirstStep` returns nothing for queued or running scoping.
- Only the seam answers wait, instead of asking the selector.
- If review prefers the literal reading, the change is one line: drop scoping from the wait.

This is not a cut, since nothing asked is undelivered, so I raised no `DECISION:`.
